source.title: New Insights into Graph Convolutional Networks using Neural Tangent Kernels
source.authors: Mahalakshmi Sabanayagam; P. Esser; Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

record.file_problem: Full paper text present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how depth, normalization, and skip connections affect GCN test performance in semi-supervised graph node classification, extending generalization-performance analysis to a graph setting not covered by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Reports qualitative test-performance results for GCN depth, normalization, and skip connections. It does not report random-label fitting, training-to-test gaps, width sweeps past interpolation, image CNN-versus-fully-connected comparisons, or the other version-specific measurements.
record.test_reason: The study measures depth, normalization, and skip-connection effects in graph node classification. None tests V1–V8. Width is tuned without establishing interpolation or a post-interpolation width trend; graph convolutions are not compared with fully connected image classifiers. NTK alignment is not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive NTKs for semi-supervised GCNs and propose them as surrogates for studying architecture and depth. Appropriate normalization stabilizes deeper vanilla GCN training, while skip connections reduce sensitivity to normalization. NTKs converge with depth for vanilla and skip architectures, with near-perfect alignment especially evident for skip connections. Skip-α is also proposed for assessing the relative importance of graph structure and node features.
record.recipe_differences: Semi-supervised binary node classification on graph datasets; evaluates GCNs and their infinite-width NTKs, including depth and normalization, rather than the claim versions' image or standard natural-label settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance changes with network depth, hidden-layer size, learning rate, normalization constant, skip-connection type, and dataset; the WebKB Skip-α depth trend differs from other datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: GCN depth-related test-performance degradation depends on normalization and hyperparameter choices; skip-connection NTKs outperform vanilla NTKs, with a distinct improving depth trend on WebKB for Skip-α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In binary graph node classification, suitable normalization and training choices can reduce depth-related GCN performance degradation, while the benefits of skip connections depend on architecture and dataset.

record.problems: The experiments use three graph datasets converted from multiclass to binary classification. Best-performance comparisons select among learning rates and hidden sizes. Several reported comparisons are qualitative in the text, with values available only in figures; the paper notes an out-of-memory issue for some Citeseer depth-128 cases and a numerical precision issue in one plotted result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately described numerical results could be extracted from the supplied text; several experiments are shown only in figures without text-stated values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond an established zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error; dropout appears only as future work.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values. All row states are assessed against V1–V8; cannot_determine here means the measures cannot establish those versions, not that the qualitative graph-classification findings are unsupported.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out comparison on natural labels.
No width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.
No image comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison to other generalization measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.
